style: Late-90s East Coast street rap, 90 BPM, hookless, the track is a numbered list. Bare dusty boom-bap: heavy swung kick, crisp cracking snare, one moody jazz keys phrase repeating in a minor key, deep sub bass. A DJ chops in a hype-man voice barking each number before its rule. Lead: big-bodied Brooklyn man rapping, deep wheezy voice from the chest, round plummy tone, unhurried conversational flow that lags a fraction late, calm threat, dry and upfront in the mix
exclude: gravelly old man voice, female vocals, high youthful voice, radio announcer, orchestral strings, spoken word poetry, trap hi-hats, 808 rolls, lo-fi chill, autotune, sung chorus, backing vocals, big reverb, cinematic swells
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.
title: tec-r2-exclude-the-wrong-voice
